subject: User-defined distribution with bounded support: log-probability

messages.author: 78efca6d80693fd9
messages.subject: User-defined distribution with bounded support: log-probability
parts:
I have about one hour's experience of nimble, so this is probably a really stupid question. I am trying to write a user-defined distribution where the support for the density function may sometimes have an upper bound or a lower bound, beyond which the density is of course zero.
Does that cause a problem when calculating the log probability, or can I just naively write log(.) ?

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: User-defined distribution with bounded support: log-probability
parts:
This certainly can be handled correctly in NIMBLE, although depending on exactly how you're using your custom-written distribution (for MCMC?), it might require a small amount of care in getting the implementation correct.

A good start will be supplying the "range" argument when you call registerDistributions, with the correct lower and upper bounds.

It would also be good to make sure your custom-written density function returns -Inf (when returning the log-density), when the random variable falls outside te support.

It will sometimes give some warning messages if you do pure R execution (e.g. using the uncompiled model object, or running an uncompiled MCMC).  But these warnings won't show up when you're using the compiled versions of the model and MCMC.

Hope this helps!

Thanks for such a quick response. 
I am using the function for MCMC.
Whether there are bounds and if so their values depend on stochastic variables in the simulation and will therefore change at each iteration. Does that rule out the idea of supplying a 'range' argument?

Within my function I can test whether any given x falls outside the bounds, and then return -Inf explicitly. I avoid calculating log(0). Is that what you had in mind?
